messages.author: 9c61751d797b50a0
messages.subject: clustered data produces "subscript out of bounds"
parts:
Hi all,

I am migrating to lavaan from Mplus and I'm fitting a multiple group model to a large data set. The "group" is country and the data are clustered in schools, so I am also defining clusters. I started with a basic specification that does not include clusters and everything goes along fine. But when I add the cluster variable, I get the error "ov.names.l[[g]] : subscript out of bounds"

I see in GitHub that lavaan was updated very recently to better estimate the log likelihood of clustered data. I'm wondering if what I am seeing is a bug?

Any thoughts are welcome. 

Leslie

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: clustered data produces "subscript out of bounds"
parts:
For now (using dev 0.6-1), just adding a cluster= argument is not
enough. You must adapt your syntax and add a level: 1 and level: 2 section.

For example:

myModel <- '
level: 1
fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
level: 2
fb =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
'

If you have no model for the between level (level 2), create a saturated
model:

myModel <- '
level: 1
fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
level: 2
y1 ~~ y2 + y3 + y4
y2 ~~ y3 + y4
y3 ~~ y4
'

This will not be needed any longer in a next update of 0.6-1, because
this will be the default behavior.

Yves.

messages.author: 5e50b609bab3f524
messages.subject: Re: clustered data produces "subscript out of bounds"
parts:
Dear Yves,

Thanks a lot for the reply.
I have tried fitting a sem model with all details specified, but I still run into the same error.

I'm following the steps of Hox to conduct a two-level CFA, with 3 latent variables and 10 items.
Model 1 converges (three-factor model at the within-level + null model at between level)
Model 2 converges as well (three-factor model at within-level + independence model at between level), returning some negative variances though
Model 3 doesn't converge, giving the error "Error in ov.names.l[[g]] : subscript out of bounds"

Also tried specifying a between-level model with a saturated individual-level model (because I think that theoretically, my construct should be seen as a shared between-level construct), but that didn't converge either (giving the same error)

I wonder if there is something wrong with my model specification, or if it could be related to Lavaan 0.6.
I'm happy to send you the syntax and relevant information in case you think this needs further investigation.

Thanks for the help,
Sarah

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: clustered data produces "subscript out of bounds"
parts:
This works for me:

library(lavaan) # must be a 0.6-1 version

FamIQData <- read.table("FamIQData.dat")
names(FamIQData) <- c("family", "child", "wordlist", "cards",
"matrices", "figures", "animals", "occupats")

model1 <- '
level: 1
numeric =~ wordlist + cards + matrices
perception =~ figures + animals + occupats
level: 2
wordlist ~~ 0*wordlist
cards ~~ 0*cards
matrices ~~ 0*matrices
figures ~~ 0*figures
animals ~~ 0*animals
occupats ~~ 0*occupats
'

fit1 <- sem(model1, data = FamIQData, cluster = "family",
std.lv = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit1)

model2 <- '
level: 1
numeric =~ wordlist + cards + matrices
perception =~ figures + animals + occupats
level: 2
wordlist ~~ wordlist
cards ~~ cards
matrices ~~ matrices
figures ~~ figures
animals ~~ animals
occupats ~~ occupats
'

fit2 <- sem(model2, data = FamIQData, cluster = "family",
std.lv = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit2)

model3 <- '
level: 1
numeric =~ wordlist + cards + matrices
perception =~ figures + animals + occupats
level: 2
# saturated
wordlist ~~ cards + matrices + figures + animals + occupats
cards ~~ matrices + figures + animals + occupats
matrices ~~ figures + animals + occupats
figures ~~ animals + occupats
animals ~~ occupats
'

fit3 <- sem(model3, data = FamIQData, cluster = "family",
std.lv = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit3)

model4a <- '
level: 1
numeric =~ wordlist + cards + matrices
perception =~ figures + animals + occupats
level: 2
general =~ wordlist + cards + matrices +
figures + animals + occupats
'

fit4a <- sem(model4a, data = FamIQData, cluster = "family",
std.lv = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit4a)


If this doesn't work for you, please show us your full R script.

Yves.
